chunks: Abu Hamzah al-Thumali narrated from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib: 'O Ja'far, shall I not grant you, shall I not give you, shall I not favor you, shall I not teach you a salat that, if you pray it, even if you had fled from the battlefield and upon you were sins like the sand of 'Alij and the foam of the sea, you would be forgiven?'

He said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He صلى الله عليه وآله said: 'You pray four rak'ahs whenever you wish: if you wish, every night; if you wish, every day; if you wish, then from one Jumu'ah to another; and if you wish, then from one month to another; and if you wish, then from one year to another. You begin the salat, then say fifteen times: Allahu Akbar, Subhan Allah, al-hamdu lillah, and la ilaha illa Allah. Then you recite al-Fatihah and a surah, and bow, and say them in your ruku' ten times. Then you raise your head from ruku' and say them ten times. Then you fall in sajdah and say them ten times in your sujud. Then you raise your head from sujud and say them ten times. Then you fall in sajdah and say them ten times. Then you raise your head from sujud and say them ten times. Then you rise and say them fifteen times. Then you recite Fatihat al-Kitab and a surah, then bow and say them ten times. Then you raise your head from ruku' and say them ten times. Then you fall in sajdah and say them ten times. Then you raise your head from sujud and say them ten times. Then you perform sajdah and say them ten times. Then you raise your head from sujud and say them ten times. Then you recite the tashahhud and conclude with taslim. Then you stand and pray two other rak'ahs, doing in them the like of that, then you conclude with taslim.'

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: 'That is seventy-five times in each rak'ah, three hundred tasbihs; in the four rak'ahs it becomes one thousand two hundred tasbihs. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, multiplies it for you and writes for you by it twelve thousand good deeds, each good deed among them being like Mount Uhud, and greater.'

key_terms.الرُّكُوعِ: The bowing position in salat where the prescribed dhikr is recited.
key_terms.السُّجُودِ: The state of prostration in salat where the prescribed dhikr is recited.
key_terms.تَسْبِيحَةٍ: A formula of glorification and remembrance repeated throughout the prayer.
key_terms.حَسَنَةٍ: A good deed, multiplied greatly as the reward for this salat.
key_terms.ذُنُوبًا: Sins, which are promised forgiveness through performing this prayer.
key_terms.رَكَعَاتٍ: Units of ritual prayer; this prayer consists of four rak'ahs.
key_terms.صَلَاةً: A special prayer taught by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله to Ja'far ibn Abi Talib.
key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: Surat al-Fatihah, recited in each rak'ah of the prayer.

ai.seo_question: How is the salat of Ja'far al-Tayyar performed and what reward is mentioned for it?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the salat of Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and describes its great merit and method in detail. It presents a supererogatory prayer built around repeated dhikr and promises immense forgiveness and multiplied reward for the one who performs it.
